newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish steel mill to choose sell-off adviser May 6.
newsitem.headline: Polish steel mill to choose sell-off adviser May 6.

text.p: The Polish government's tender commission is likely to choose a firm advising on the privatisation of the country's largest steel mill, Huta im. Sendzimira SA, on Tuesday, the mill's president said.

"On May 6, the tender commission will most probably decide on the privatisation adviser which would prepare a legal and financial audit and estimate the value of the firm," Jerzy Knapik told reporters on Monday.

He confirmed that under the Sendzimir privatisation programme three daughter companies should be carved out from the firm this year and later separately privatised through sales of equity to strategic investors.

Knapik named the three companies -- due to be controlled by a parent firm, which was likely to retain a majority of votes at shareholders' meetings -- as the steel mill, power house and electric works.
Knapik said that a stake in the power house, for which more than 10 investors are bidding, would be sold this year and equity in the two other firms later on.

He said three investors from the steel sector has responded positively to the company's invitation for negotiations. Two firms from the financial sector are ready to invest in the steel mill along with a strategic investor.
Earlier this year, Knapik said that it could prove difficult to find an investor in the mill, which would be content with only a minority stake in the company.
He then said Sendzimir's steel mills needed about $200 million in investment to face foreign competition after Poland lifts barriers protecting its steel sector in the next several years.

Sendzimir, based near the southern city of Krakow, saw its net profit fall to about 14.3 million zlotys last year from 100 million in 1995 due to a harsh winter and the bad climate in steel industry. The company had sales of 2.9 billion zlotys in 1996.
The firm employing 17,500 workers, produced 2.5 million tonnes of steel last year.
Knapik also said his company was likely to increase its commercial papers programme this year to 50 million zlotys from the current 25 million zlotys.
